text:
I have known about this for quite some time, and the more I think about it, the more useless it seems. Sure, the underlying machine operation is just addition, which is indeed commutative, but at the type system level, the pointer and the offset have distinct roles. It just makes no sense to allow to commute them, just like it makes no sense to allow to commute arguments to, say, strchr, just because the compiler can figure it out by looking at the types. When was the last time you had a practical reason to write "offset + pointer" or "index[array]"?

In most languages, the indexing operator is not commutative. In Rust (alas, not that many languages with pointer arithmetic), pointer offseting is expressed as a function call or a method, also not commutative. I have never seen a single complaint about either. It's not something people want or care about, it's just a tedious detail.
